A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CLUE research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including material relocated or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: V1 reports original automatic evaluations on HealthVer and DRUID and a 12-participant human evaluation.

after.justification: V2 retains those original results and adds relation-labeler experiments, error analysis, computational measurements, and extended evaluations.

M1.justification: The core entropy-scoring, span-extraction, prompting, and attention-steering pipeline is retained. V2 adds a tested Qwen alternative to GPT-4o relation labeling and adapts the three-evidence setting to select one interaction from each of six input-part pairs.

E1.justification: HealthVer, DRUID, and English fact-checking remain the coverage. Appendix H.1 adds a HealthVer scenario with three evidence passages per claim, extending the original two-evidence input conditions.

E2.justification: The main comparisons retain PromptBaseline, CLUE-Span, and CLUE-Span+Steering. V2 additionally compares GPT-4o against Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct as relation labelers under otherwise fixed CLUE settings in Appendix C.2, Table 4.

E3.justification: V2 adds controlled labeler-swap and manual-audit protocols, DeepSeek backbone evaluation, a six-interaction three-evidence configuration, resource profiling, and pooled first-place human-preference reporting. It also changes the reported hardware from four 40GB A100s to one 80GB A100 and corrects seven insertion sites to four; the stated 12 perturbations per instance remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds a relation-labeler ablation and an upstream-error audit of 50 HealthVer instances and 150 span pairs. Appendix C.3 reports 86% labeling accuracy and propagation of 13 of 21 mislabeled interactions into explanations. Three-evidence testing and computational-overhead analyses further expand the supplementary evaluation.

E5.justification: Both versions report 7,200 perturbation observations per dataset, the same correlation t-tests and significance thresholds, and Kendall's W for human agreement. V2 corrects the number of significant CLUE-Span correlations, but does not change the statistical procedure or add repeated-run, seed, or confidence-interval reporting.

E6.justification: All 60 numerical values in the main automatic-results table and all 45 original human mean-rank values are unchanged. V2 adds labeler, error-audit, runtime, memory, three-evidence, DeepSeek, and pooled preference results. It also corrects the stated count of significant CLUE-Span correlations from three to two.

T1.justification: The uncertainty, span-importance, steering, Entropy-CCT, and significance-test mathematics are retained. V2 expands the explanation of the existing TVD comparison and renumbers equations without adding substantive mathematical definitions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: Both versions claim an inference-time framework explaining predictive uncertainty through evidence conflicts and agreements, with improved faithfulness, label consistency, and human-rated quality. The revised abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain this contribution and its general applicability claim.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive discussion of fragmentary spans, relation-label errors, downstream propagation, and the scope of its white-box transparency. It interprets the new evidence-count and reasoning-model results and explicitly limits conclusions about usefulness relative to numerical confidence or hedges. Human results receive a stronger, pooled 'approximately twice as often' preference interpretation.

D1.justification: New Appendix E documents stage-level latency, GPU memory, steering requirements, and GPT-4o token and cost estimates. Appendix F.1 specifies the spaCy model and NLTK/WordNet candidate construction, while Appendix I.1 expands study randomization and filtering details. These materially extend the earlier implementation disclosures.

R1.justification: V2 adds discussion of graph-guided and self-refined explanations, related summarization work, and uncertainty-explanation user research, including Yuan et al. (2025), Wang and Atanasova (2025), and Warren et al. (2026). The earlier ROUGE/BLEU discussion is removed, while the central positioning against verdict-oriented explanations remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and related-work narrative are substantially rewritten. Related Work moves from Section 2 to Section 6, faithfulness appendices are consolidated, and detailed human-variant results move to the appendix. Method explanations and terminology also receive extensive editing.

P2.justification: V2 restructures Table 1, moves the original human mean-rank table to Table 11, and introduces a pooled-preference main table. New tables display labeler, runtime, memory, three-evidence, and reasoning-model results. Figures 1–2 receive caption or annotation revisions, with substantial accompanying layout changes.

improvement.justification: The new labeler ablation, error audit, extended tests, and resource disclosures strengthen transparency and applicability evidence. However, v2's stronger human-preference framing pools two CLUE options against one baseline despite unchanged individual rankings, and its DeepSeek discussion overstates superiority across metrics. These weaknesses limit the net gain from the useful additional evidence.
